summary: Mounting the yaw servo from below works. I checked the geometry: the shelf is a solid 7 mm round all four M3 tap holes (8 mm screws, 5.5 mm engaged). The 21 x 55 mm opening in the floor passes the tabs. The rear screws take a straight key and the two beside the boss take a ball-end key in the widened pocket. The tab underside is still at z_shelf (33.3), so the horn and gear heights (horn face 53.7, gear screws at 54.4) have not moved. The base FEA hot spots are on the bearing tower and a front bolt foot, at 0.95 MPa against a 13 MPa limit. The stall FEA now runs with case crash and SF 3, and the hood web is fixed. However, the widening that gives key access pushed the housing's -Y wall out to y = -26. The new yaw lead exit (x -38.4..-30.4) now opens against the inside of the gear guard ring, only 0.7 to 3.4 mm away. That is one printed part, so the servo's 3-pin plug (at least 7.6 mm wide at 2.54 mm pitch) cannot get out of the pocket to the guard hole. The yaw servo cannot be wired as the design describes.

findings.issue: The yaw lead exit faces the guard ring with almost no gap. I measured the base STL in world coordinates at z = 10, 20 and 50. Between the widened housing's -Y outer face (y = -26.0) and the guard ring's inner face (r 30 about (-45, 0)), the gap is 3.4 mm at x = -38, 2.4 mm at x = -34, 1.2 mm at x = -31 and 0.7 mm at x = -30. The exit box (x -38.4..-30.4, y -27..-21, z 6..14) opens straight into that wedge, and you can see it in part_base_top.png. The guard hole (x -51..-39) is offset in X from the exit, so the lead would have to leave the exit and turn 90 degrees inside a gap of 3 mm or less. The servo's own lead ends in a 3-pin JR/Futaba plug, at least 7.6 mm wide at the catalog's 2.54 mm pitch, and the plug has to get from inside the pocket to outside the ring. The wedge is open only from the top, and it is too narrow for the plug at any height. DESIGN.md step 2 ('Lead out through the pocket's -Y exit and the guard hole') cannot be done without de-pinning the connector. The wiring route check passes only because it treats the lead as a thin polyline: waypoint [-36, -27.2, 10] sits 1.2 mm from the housing and 1.4 mm from the ring. This came in with the round-6 widening. In round 5 the housing face was at y = -14.5 and the lead ran in a channel more than 10 mm wide.
findings.fix: Make the lead's path a straight line a plug can pass. Option A: put the exit coaxial with the guard hole. Run one straight -Y cut through the housing wall and the ring at about x = -43 (inside the guard hole's x -51..-39), at least 10 mm wide and 10 mm tall, from the pocket floor up. This may mean starting the widened pocket at x = -47 so the cut opens into it. Option B: make both the exit and the guard hole slots open to the underside (cut from z = -1). The lead is then laid in from below with the base on its back, before the servo screws go in, and nothing has to be threaded. With either option, re-route pwr_yaw and sig_yaw through it. Consider teaching the wiring route check a lead/plug cross-section so a pinch like this fails kerf check.

findings.issue: base.py hard-codes the cable boss protrusion as 6.6 mm (boss_x1 = xc + L/2 + 6.6 + 0.6). The catalog's servos.MG996R value is now cable_boss_protrusion 7.0, and its note lists 6.6 as a replaced value. The boss envelope reaches xc + 27.45 and the pocket ends at xc + 27.65, which leaves 0.2 mm instead of the intended 0.6. It still clears, but it goes against the rule that purchased-part dimensions come from the catalog.
findings.fix: Read d['cable_boss_protrusion'] (or the catalog key) instead of 6.6, keep the +0.6 clearance, and re-check.

findings.issue: The last two route points of pwr_yaw and sig_yaw are [-34.4, -12, 10] and then [-55.2, 0, 27.8], the servo body centre. The drawn lead passes through the MG996R case, which also makes ASSEMBLY.md step 11 misleading. The real lead leaves the boss at about (-28, 0, 9..17).
findings.fix: End the route at the cable boss (a 'lead' joint on the servo proxy at the boss), or add that point as the last waypoint.

findings.issue: In the upright print, the shelf underside is the face the tab tops clamp against, and it is printed over support across the open pocket. The access ceiling at z_shelf - 0.5 (44 x 13 mm) is also supported. A rough supported face under the tabs can let the servo rock slightly once the screws are snug.
findings.fix: Use a support interface layer (or a PETG/PLA interface) under the shelf, and file the tab face flat before fitting the servo. Say so in DESIGN.md step 2.

findings.issue: Round-5 items verified. The pot hole is now 7 mm and the LED hole 2.5 mm (web 6.007 - 3.5 - 1.25 = 1.26 mm), and the two holes show separate in part_psu_hood_top.png. The note now says to tie the DC bundle to the bridge before seating the hood. The optional 45 degree chamfer on the bridge's -X underside was not done, so the 6 x 5 mm overhang will still sag slightly.
findings.fix: Optional: chamfer the bridge block's -X underside at 45 degrees.

findings.issue: Carried over from round 5. kerf/electrical.py still does not use the ATO fuse's catalog cold_resistance_ohm (about 45 mV at 2.5 A) or the holder's 16 AWG lead, and no servo catalog entry has a sourced lead gauge. Margin is still positive: the worst stall row is about 151 mV above 4.8 V, against roughly 60-110 mV of omitted drop.
findings.fix: Engine: add the fuse's cold resistance and the holder lead to the run's loop resistance, and add a sourced lead gauge to the servo entries.

findings.issue: Carried over: 12.6 % of the surface prints on support, so the support side of the column will be rough. Cosmetic.
findings.fix: Optional: set the column flush with one long side of the foot so it lies on the bed with no support.

findings.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the WAGO splices and the inline fuse holders sit loose on the desk behind the base.
findings.fix: None required. A printed electronics tray on the rear pad would be tidier and short-proof.

findings.issue: For the record: at the new crash-case SF 3, upper_arm_stall_fea p99.9 is 13.42 MPa against a 16 MPa limit (a margin of 1.19). The peak of 18.76 MPa is a local singularity at the frame of the elbow servo window in plate A, which is on the load path in the render. It passes, but it is the thinnest margin on the arm. The DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.
findings.fix: None required. Test-print yoke_r and the upper arm and fit the real DS3225/DS3218 before printing the rest, as the Risks section of DESIGN.md says.
